title: Finite-type approximation models and the base colimit
statement: Let φ : R → S be a finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. There exist a small nonempty directed preorder Λ, functors Rfun,Sfun : Λ → CommRing, a natural transformation η : Rfun → Sfun, and cocones cR,cS with points R,S. Their legs satisfy κ_l η_l = φ π_l. Each η_l is finite type, and each R_l is finite type over ℤ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Every transition square and every square with the final map φ is a pushout. The base cocone cR is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No colimit property for cS is asserted.

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation $\Phi:R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ as an $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $C\subseteq R$ be the $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra generated by all coefficients of the finitely many $f_j$. Each polynomial has finite support, so this is a finite set of coefficients, including when $n=0$ or $m=0$. Write $f_{j,T}\in T[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ for the same expression whenever $C\subseteq T\subseteq R$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00R0 (lemma-limit-finite-presentation), proof referring to Tag 00QV (lemma-limit-essentially-finite-presentation), first paragraph: a finite list of relation polynomials and their coefficients

proof.text: Let $\Lambda$ be the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras $T\subseteq R$ containing $C$, ordered by inclusion. It contains $C$. Given $T,U\in\Lambda$, the subalgebra generated by their finite generating sets contains both, so $\Lambda$ is directed. Every $r\in R$ belongs to the member generated by $C\cup\{r\}$, and the transition maps are inclusions. Thus $(R,(T\hookrightarrow R)_{T\in\Lambda})$ is a colimit of the $T$ in commutative rings by [lemma-nagata-ring-finite-type-subalgebras], restricting its full directed system to this cofinal subsystem. Put $R_T=T$; each is a finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Lemma Tag 00R0 (lemma-limit-finite-presentation), clauses (1),(2); construction of a directed coefficient system in the proof of Tag 00QV (lemma-limit-essentially-finite-presentation)

proof.text: For $T\in\Lambda$ set $S_T=T[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_{1,T},\ldots,f_{m,T})$ and let $\rho_T:T\to S_T$ be the structure map. The inclusion $T\subseteq U$ sends every $f_{j,T}$ to $f_{j,U}$, hence induces a ring map $S_T\to S_U$ compatible with $\rho_T$; identities and compositions agree because these maps agree on $T$ and the classes of all $x_i$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Coefficient inclusion also gives $\kappa_T:S_T\to S$ through $\Phi$, compatible with these maps and satisfying $\kappa_T\rho_T=\varphi|_T$. Each $S_T$ is generated as a $T$-algebra by the $n$ classes of $x_i$, proving clause (3).

source.place: Lemma Tag 00R0 (lemma-limit-finite-presentation), clauses (3),(4), following the displayed polynomial quotient system in the proof of Tag 00QV

proof.text: Fix $T\subseteq U$ in $\Lambda$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension], $S_T\otimes_TU$ is the quotient of $U[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ by the extended ideal generated by $f_{1,T},\ldots,f_{m,T}$: explicitly, the maps $U[x]\to S_T\otimes_TU$, $u\mapsto1\otimes u$, $x_i\mapsto\bar x_i\otimes1$, and $S_T\otimes_TU\to U[x]/(f_{1,U},\ldots,f_{m,U})$, $\bar p\otimes u\mapsto u\bar p$, respect all relations. Each map descends through the indicated quotient [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and their composites fix $U$ and every $x_i$, so they are inverse $U$-algebra maps. The latter is exactly the canonical map $S_T\otimes_TU\to S_U$, proving (4).

source.place: Lemma Tag 00R0 (lemma-limit-finite-presentation), clause (4), obtained by omitting the localization from the polynomial quotient construction in the proof of Tag 00QV

proof.text: The same two explicit maps with $U=R$ identify $S_T\otimes_TR$ with $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$, and composing with $\Phi$ gives the map $s\otimes r\mapsto\kappa_T(s)\varphi(r)$ of (5). In particular it is an isomorphism for every $T\in\Lambda$.

theorem exists_limit_finite_presentation_core
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (hφ : RingHom.FinitePresentation φ) :
    ∃ (Λ : Type u) (_hpo : Preorder Λ) (_hne : Nonempty Λ)
      (_hdir : IsDirected Λ (fun a b => a ≤ b))
      (Rfun : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat) (Sfun : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat)
      (η : Rfun ⟶ Sfun) (cR : Cocone Rfun) (cS : Cocone Sfun),
      cR.pt = CommRingCat.of R ∧ cS.pt = CommRingCat.of S ∧
      (∀ l (hR : cR.pt = CommRingCat.of R) (hS : cS.pt = CommRingCat.of S),
        η.app l ≫ cS.ι.app l = cR.ι.app l ≫
          (eqToHom hR ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom φ ≫ eqToHom hS.symm)) ∧
      (∀ l, RingHom.FiniteType (η.app l).hom) ∧
      (∀ l, RingHom.FiniteType (algebraMap ℤ (Rfun.obj l))) ∧
      (∀ l m (h : l ≤ m),
        Nonempty (CategoryTheory.IsPushout (η.app l) (Rfun.map (homOfLE h))
          (Sfun.map (homOfLE h)) (η.app m))) ∧
      (∀ l (hR : cR.pt = CommRingCat.of R) (hS : cS.pt = CommRingCat.of S),
        Nonempty (CategoryTheory.IsPushout (η.app l) (cR.ι.app l) (cS.ι.app l)
          (eqToHom hR ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom φ ≫ eqToHom hS.symm))) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit cR)
